question.explanation:
First, let's recall the sum and difference formulas for cosine: \begin{align*} \cos(\alpha-\beta) &= \cos \alpha \cos \beta + \sin \alpha \sin \beta \\[5pt] \cos(\alpha+\beta) &= \cos \alpha \cos \beta - \sin \alpha \sin \beta \end{align*}

Adding these equations, we get the following product-to-sum identity: \begin{align*} \cos(\alpha-\beta) + \cos(\alpha+\beta) &= 2 \cos \alpha \cos \beta \\[5pt] \cos \alpha \cos \beta &= \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \cos(\alpha-\beta) + \cos(\alpha+\beta) \right) \end{align*}

Thus, we have \begin{align*} \cos(2x)\cos(5x) &= \dfrac{1}{2}\big(\cos(2x-5x)+\cos(2x+5x)\big) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}\big(\cos(-3x)+\cos(7x)\big) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}\big(\cos(3x)+\cos(7x)\big). \end{align*}

Substituting this into the integral gives \begin{align*} \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \cos(2x)\cos(5x)\,\text{d}x &= \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \dfrac{1}{2}\cos(3x)+\dfrac{1}{2}\cos(7x)\:\text{d}x \\[5pt] &= \left[ \dfrac{1}{6} \sin(3x)+\dfrac{1}{14}\sin(7x)\right]_{0}^{\pi/2} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{6}\left(\sin\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)-\sin(0)\right)+\dfrac{1}{14}\left(\sin\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{2}\right)-\sin(0)\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{6}(-1-0)+\dfrac{1}{14}(-1-0) \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{-\dfrac{5}{21}}. \end{align*}

question.explanation:
First, let's recall the sum and difference formulas for sine: \begin{align*} \sin(\alpha+\beta) &= \sin \alpha \cos \beta + \cos \alpha \sin \beta \\[5pt] \sin(\alpha-\beta) &= \sin \alpha \cos \beta - \cos \alpha \sin \beta \end{align*}

Adding these equations, we get the following product-to-sum identity: \begin{align*} \sin(\alpha+\beta) + \sin(\alpha-\beta) &= 2 \sin\alpha \cos\beta \\[5pt] \sin\alpha \cos\beta &= \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \sin(\alpha+\beta) + \sin(\alpha-\beta) \right) \end{align*}

Thus, we have \begin{align*} \sin(9x)\cos(3x) &= \dfrac{1}{2}\big(\sin(9x+3x)+\sin(9x-3x)\big) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}\big(\sin(12x)+\sin(6x)\big). \end{align*}

Substituting this into the integral gives \begin{align*} \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin(9x)\cos(3x)\,\text{d}x &= \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \dfrac{1}{2}\sin(12x)+\dfrac{1}{2}\sin(6x)\:\text{d}x \\[5pt] &= \left[ -\dfrac{1}{24} \cos(12x)-\dfrac{1}{12}\cos(6x)\right]_{0}^{\pi/2} \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{1}{24}\left(\cos(6\pi)-\cos(0)\right)-\dfrac{1}{12}\left(\cos(3\pi)-\cos(0)\right) \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{1}{24}(1-1)-\dfrac{1}{12}(-1-1) \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{\dfrac{1}{6}}. \end{align*}

example.title: Integrating a Product of Sine and Cosine

question.explanation:
First, let's recall the sum and difference formulas for sine: \begin{align*} \sin(\alpha+\beta) &= \sin \alpha \cos \beta + \cos \alpha \sin \beta \\[5pt] \sin(\alpha-\beta) &= \sin \alpha \cos \beta - \cos \alpha \sin \beta \end{align*}

Adding these equations, we get the following product-to-sum identity: \begin{align*} \sin(\alpha+\beta) + \sin(\alpha-\beta) &= 2 \sin\alpha \cos\beta \\[5pt] \sin\alpha \cos\beta &= \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \sin(\alpha+\beta) + \sin(\alpha-\beta) \right) \end{align*}

Thus, we have \begin{align*} \sin(3x)\cos(6x) &= \dfrac{1}{2}\big(\sin(3x+6x)+\sin(3x-6x)\big) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}\big(\sin(9x)+\sin(-3x)\big) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}\big(\sin(9x)-\sin(3x)\big). \end{align*}

Substituting this into the integral gives \begin{align*} \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin(3x)\cos(6x)\,\text{d}x &= \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \dfrac{1}{2}\sin(9x)-\dfrac{1}{2}\sin(3x)\:\text{d}x \\[5pt] &= \left[ -\dfrac{1}{18} \cos(9x)+\dfrac{1}{6}\cos(3x)\right]_{0}^{\pi/2} \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{1}{18}\left(\cos\left(\dfrac{9\pi}{2}\right)-\cos(0)\right)+\dfrac{1}{6}\left(\cos\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)-\cos(0)\right) \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{1}{18}(0-1)+\dfrac{1}{6}(0-1) \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{-\dfrac{1}{9}}. \end{align*}

Thus, we have \begin{align*} \sin(10x)\cos(4x) &= \dfrac{1}{2}\big(\sin(10x+4x)+\sin(10x-4x)\big) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}\big(\sin(14x)+\sin(6x)\big). \end{align*}
